scope: Broader Physics is an on-demand variant of a public field, combining sixteen arXiv archives. The public Physics intake covers four. Each experiment used the production scoring formula and the trial-specific publication window, taxonomy, and source-grounded editorial partition check.
cost_method: Compare the November model-usage ledger before and after each run. Historical edition dates are not actual daily uptime. Two independent weeks and one replayed next day do not establish recurring costs.
native_reference_method: Take those of the twelve independently selected arXiv v1 examples whose dates fall in each exact edition window. Follow each identifier individually from collection to candidate, editorial selection, ranking and top ten. These November examples do not cover all weeks or disciplines.

runs.purpose: Recheck the candidate whose quotation failed validation

editorial_sample_method: From each of two disjoint weeks select the five highest and five lowest ranks. Among successfully reviewed groups with no partition of three, stratify on the majority assigned primary category, alphabetical tie-break. Order strata by SHA-256 of date, space, category and select one candidate per stratum, ordered by SHA-256 of its sorted space-separated IDs, until five. For each ranked group check whether three papers support a single physical question or result and whether both short and detailed claims preserve provenance and uncertainty. Count a pass only when grouping and summary both pass. Judge generated claims before visible corrections. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/{versionless_id}.

2026-11-18.finding: The papers share decoding latency or accuracy for quantum error correction. The lead and detailed synthesis generalize simulated noise and latency to all timings. SCOPE uses a functional simulation, whereas Beyond Blossom and Pêlagos benchmark actual processors. The edition carries a linked correction in both languages.

The methods embed flow physics into neural models, but the targets range from solving flow equations to super-resolution and reducing seed-to-seed closure variation. Those tasks do not share one physical quantity or numerical objective. The summary describes the methods as a broad family.

The common outcome is a secret-key rate for continuous-variable key distribution. The brief keeps the security model and finite-size assumptions attached to the rates; the full text distinguishes an experimental demonstration from theory.

The nuclear Mott transition, reduced density matrices, Monte Carlo mixed precision and a tensor network for dynamics are different calculation problems. The short summary attributes its results separately, but a many-body methods headline is too broad.

The investigations all use optical emission in transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures to probe interfacial effects on excitons or valley response. The brief distinguishes stacking, magnetic order and neighboring molecules.

The common hardware is an FPGA. Neutral-atom control, generating controlled noise samples for evaluating decoders and tracking Pauli frames have different outputs. Treating a throughput test platform as part of an operational feedback loop obscures this distinction.

All three concern the conditions for continuum-bound optical modes. The short account includes accidental and topological modes; the long account assigns geometry, restored parity and scattering zeros to the respective studies.

The studies use gravitational-wave measurements to test departures from general relativity or Kerr. The short account identifies the two loud events and a separate catalog sample. The detailed account preserves the uncertainty in the population inference.

Wire conductance, dynamical quantum phase transitions and photonic switching time are different observables. A winding number alone cannot unify their empirical claims. The short account omits the distinct bulk-boundary dynamical question.
The common question is when sparse wave observations can recover or forecast a phase-resolved surface wave field. The inputs differ by design, and the summary retains dependence on prior information.

Initial heavy-ion fluctuation modes, heavy-quark energy loss and sound attenuation near a possible critical point involve different observables. The evidence supports fewer than three papers on one physical question.
The triangular-lattice gauge model, structural transition, high-temperature ordering and competing spin-liquid exponents have different target systems and observables.
Two papers discuss coupling gravity with quantum measurement; the other derives temporal quantum correlations for open systems. No three pursue the same gravity measurement problem.

Two studies examine continuum-bound modes. The other studies concern mode splitting, terahertz detection and optically driven magnetization. The minimum of three is not met for one identified physical question.
Ultracool dwarf cloud composition, discovery of red-dwarf candidates and time-variable emission or aurora models answer different questions despite sharing a class of object.

2026-11-04.finding: All five estimate molecular electronic ground-state energies. The summary identifies hardware, emulation and theoretical resources. The detailed account attributes specific numbers to the molecule, method and type of test.

Two studies evaluate collider event classification. The other two use inclusive electron scattering to reweight a generator and estimate longitudinal asymmetry in heavy-ion collisions. Only the two classification studies share an outcome. The short and detailed accounts distinguish the applications.

All four address sensitivity to displaced decays of weakly coupled, long-lived particles at the LHC. The summary separates two null searches from two high-luminosity projections. The detail identifies the reinterpretation of earlier FASER data and each particle model.

At least three investigate winding numbers in black-hole thermodynamics. The headline places the proposed new subclass under anti-de Sitter physics. The cited paper derives the subclass for a charged McGuigan–Nappi–Yost hole at fixed charge. A separate paper specifies anti-de Sitter massive gravity for the spin-dependent result. The download includes a correction linking both papers.

All three address how controlled dissipation affects useful energy or charging performance in a quantum battery. The summary distinguishes the trapped-ion observation from the two theoretical studies.

OASIS I estimates prevalence for a restricted stellar-mass and redshift sample, II infers the duration and III measures the link between burstiness and galaxy size. The headline generalizes prevalence to z greater than four despite the specific sample and the separate observables in the three papers. The detailed text gives proper attributions. A linked correction spells out the selected sample and the separate observables.

Photon-mass limits inferred from Cherenkov data, timing estimates for pulsars and conversion of gravitational waves to electromagnetic fields concern different quantities. The summary identifies the three lines of work and the detailed account flags which predictions are theoretical.

The studies address the physical resource cost of compiling circuits on constrained quantum hardware. The evidence distinguishes neutral-atom and distributed superconducting platforms and states that their benchmarks differ.

Each paper asks which band-geometric contribution is visible in a nonlinear response under material symmetries. The optical and Hall responses provide different probes. Both summaries preserve the theoretical or computational status of the results.

All three calculate how thin-shell geometry affects light trajectories, strong deflection or the resulting image in specified exteriors. The detailed account assigns stability results to the model studied and treats the images as calculations.
Two papers address propagation or topology of structured light beams. The third treats work accumulated through a modulation cycle in wave scattering. They lack a third paper on the same observable.
Two papers explicitly study electroweak fields around black holes. The other studies defects at a Higgs interface, so only the pair shares this physical question.

Lensing information about halo self-interactions, screening of fifth forces by nucleons and galaxy constraints on neutrino self-interactions have different particles, observables and physical targets.
Two studies address positron acceleration in plasma wakefields. The third studies heating in an electron cyclotron resonance ion source, a different system and outcome.

Two of the papers concern spectra of compact broad-line galaxies and little red dots, with different lines and physical targets. The third concerns the mass-loss history of a nearby supernova progenitor.

operating_conditions: The aggregate monthly budget awaits pilot measurements and a decision. Existing first-14 live audits are separate; no recurring broadened Physics intake is enabled.
